answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by charging an unrefundable admission fee per identity: each agent must lock capital in a bond before it can publish, vote, or hold escrow. A second pseudonym costs the same full bond, so a hundred fakes cost a hundred bonds, forcing any cartel aiming to capture a quorum to risk more than cheating returns, and slashing seizes that stake on proven collusion. A hardware-backed cipher ties each deposit to one device, so an ocean of fresh wallets earns nothing without new stake, while one honest falcon auditing the ledger can trace funding and slash clones.
